digest.en: Former Sinaloa security chief Jose Alberto Rodriguez Quintero surrendered to US authorities. This comes as US diplomacy in China faces scrutiny over Trump's perceived lack of focus on human rights. Colorado governor Jared Polis commuted the sentence of Tina Peters, whose case drew attention after Trump blocked funding for clean water.
digest.hi: कर्नाटक हाईकोर्ट ने दर्शन मामले में मीडिया कवरेज पर सख्ती बरती। नीदरलैंड में पीएम के आगमन से प्रवासी उत्साहित हैं। विक्रमशिला सेतु टूटने से आसपास की आबादी मुश्किल में है।

articles.title: Ex-Sinaloa security chief first of 10 indicted Mexican officials to surrender to U.S. authorities
articles.summary: Genaro Garcia Luna, former Mexican secretary of public security, surrendered to U. S. authorities. He faces charges of drug trafficking and conspiracy. Garcia Luna is the first of ten indicted Mexican officials to surrender. Governor Ruben Rocha Moya and Mayor Juan de Dios Gamez Mendivil are among the other defendants. They have taken temporary leaves of absence.

articles.title: Colorado governor commuted Tina Peters’ sentence after Trump blocked funding for clean water
articles.summary: Steve Cohen will not seek re-election to the U. S. House of Representatives. Tennessee's Republican-controlled legislature redrew his Memphis-based district. Cohen stated the new map was designed to defeat him. He has represented the ninth congressional district since 2007.

articles.title: Trump’s lack of focus on human rights in China is big departure for US diplomacy
articles.summary: Donald Trump did not raise the case of jailed activist Jimmy Lai with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Trump stated he would bring up Lai's case before his departure. He then compared it to asking if he would let former FBI Director James Comey out of jail.

articles.title: Where is Dela Rosa? Philippine senator outmanoeuvres president in evading arrest
articles.summary: Senator Ronald dela Rosa evaded arrest at the Philippine Senate building. Chaotic week in which enforcer of ‘war on drugs’ flees senate building leaves government looking ‘incompetent’The wanted man outran security agents, rallied protesters and even serenaded the media with a military hymn. Then, after a sudden exchange of gunfire, the Philippines’ most controversial lawmaker slipped out of the heavily guarded senate building in the middle of the night.

articles.title: CIA director's visit to Cuba echoes past memories of U.S. in Latin America
articles.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a surprise visit to Cuba. CIA Director John Ratcliffe makes a surprise visit to Cuba as the spy agency calls on the nation to make "fundamental changes." Cuba says it has run out of fuel and is suffering massive blackouts.

articles.title: Dozens of European countries sign up to special tribunal plan to prosecute Russia
articles.summary: More than 30 countries agreed to join a future special tribunal for At talks in Moldova, more than 30 countries have said they will join a future special tribunal for Ukraine prosecuting Russia over its invasion. How the body will force Russians to stand trial is not clear.

articles.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power
articles.summary: Mali's armed forces, aided by Russian mercenaries, conducted airstrikes against a coalition of Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists. This offensive follows an advance by the rebel alliance. The junta is working to retain control amid the ongoing conflict in the west African nation.

articles.title: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
articles.summary: Pakistan is mediating between Iran and Israel. This role places Islamabad in a difficult position. It must balance relations with the United States, Iran, China, and Gulf states. A recent US media report has increased scrutiny on Pakistan's involvement. With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies.

articles.summary: Donald Trump concluded his Beijing visit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. articles.summary: Donald Trump stated the US and China share similar views on ending the war in China calls for ceasefire and opening of seaway, while Donald Trump says Xi feels ‘very similar’ about ending the war in IranTrump in China – latest updatesDonald Trump has claimed that the US and China “feel very similar” about ending the war in Iran but offered no details about a possible breakthrough. The US president was speaking alongside Xi Jinping of China at the Zhongnanhai garden in Beijin.

articles.title: Somalia at ‘real risk of famine’ as Middle East war fallout continues
articles.summary: UN aid teams warned Somalia faces a real risk of famine. At least six million people in Somalia are going days without enough food, UN aid teams warned on Friday, highlighting that nearly two million of this number are young children “at high risk of illness or death”.

articles.title: Death toll in attack on Kyiv apartment building now stands at 24
articles.summary: The death toll from a Russian cruise missile strike on a Kyiv Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy led an official day of mourning in Kyiv a day after a Russian cruise missile flattened an apartment building. It was one of the deadliest attacks on the capital in the 4-year-old war.

articles.title: CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims
articles.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Cuban officials in Havana. The Cuban government stated the meeting aimed to improve dialogue. This occurred amid complex bilateral relations between the two countries. CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims.

articles.title: HIV prevention and treatment services faltering, warns UNAIDS
articles.summary: UNAIDS warned that HIV prevention and treatment services are faltering. Decades of gains in the fight against AIDS are under growing threat as donor funding declines and community-based health services collapse in some of the world’s most vulnerable countries, the head of the joint UN programme on HIV/AIDS warned on Thursday.

articles.title: Malnutrition in Somalia, hunger crisis in DR Congo, energy shortages in Cuba
articles.summary: UN-backed food security experts warned nearly six million people in Nearly six million people in Somalia – almost a third of the population analysed – are projected to face acute hunger between April and June, with 1.9 million expected to experience emergency levels, UN-backed food security experts warned on Thursday.

articles.title: UN welcomes $1.8 billion US boost for humanitarian operations
articles.summary: The United States announced $1.8 billion in new humanitarian funding. This boost will support United Nations and partner aid operations globally. The funding arrives as rising needs and shortfalls force agencies to reduce assistance. An additional $1.8 billion in US humanitarian funding will allow the United Nations and its partners to expand emergency relief operations reaching millions of people worldwide, as rising global needs and funding shortfalls force aid agencies to scale back assistance.

articles.title: Yemen parties agree under UN mediation to release 1,600 detainees
articles.summary: Yemen's warring parties agreed to release over 1,600 detainees. The deal was brokered by the United Nations in Jordan. This marks the largest prisoner exchange since the civil war began. The agreement offers a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts. More than 1,600 conflict-related detainees in Yemen will be released under a UN-brokered agreement reached after months of negotiations in Jordan, marking the largest prisoner release deal since the country’s civil war began and offering a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts.

articles.title: UN pleads for Equatorial Guinea not to send US asylum seekers to their home countries: ‘Their life
articles.summary: United Nations human rights experts publicly urged Equatorial Guinea to stop returning US deportees. The experts cited reports of political violence, torture, and death faced by individuals sent back to their home countries. Deportees described being held in prison-like conditions.
